title: Contextual economics: pocket notebook — freshness, cache, and cost heuristics
content:
Quick context: this is my scratchpad for thinking about the tradeoff space between token-level freshness, KV/prefix caching, and per-request unit economics. Goal is an experimental plan + practical heuristics we can try on a small Redwood Dedicated pool (p2-small equivalent) before proposing API-level defaults.

Top-level hypothesis:
- Small amounts of proactive refresh and cheap freshness signals can recover a majority (>70%) of user-visible correctness without blowing token costs.
- There is a Pareto frontier: cheap freshness checks (single-turn embeddings or metadata hash) vs longer prefix re-sends. Find operating points.

Papers & quick takeaways (skim -> notes):
1) "FreshCache: Freshness-Aware KV for Conversational LMs" (arXiv 2026) — main idea: maintain per-conversation freshness score and evict prefixes when freshness falls below threshold; show 10–30% reduction in tokens for same exactness metric.
   - Notes: freshness computed from user edits/edits-per-minute + embedding delta.
   - Critique: experiments are synthetic (wiki edits); needs evaluation on noisy chat logs.

2) "Slot Memory for Dialogue: compact slots + recency weighting" (conference talk, MLR 2026)
   - Idea: compress recent turns into fixed-size slot embeddings and only append slot-ids to prompt; model is trained to read slots on demand.
   - Practical: requires model-side changes or a small reranker; heavy lift for hosted customers but good for Private deployments.

3) Lightweight eval paper: "Turn-level semantic drift metric" (workshop)
   - Metric: pairwise similarity between model output and human reference across time windows + hallucination penalty.
   - Useful as an automated monitor for freshness-related regressions.

Short experiment sketches (cheap -> more effort):
A) Freshness probe (10k chats sample)
   - For each chat, compute: (1) last-turn embedding distance to earlier turns, (2) turn edit flag (user-specified "update" messages), (3) time delta.
   - Heuristic: if embedding-dist > T or edit flag true, do full-prefix send; else use KV prefix.
   - Measurement: success = no hallucination on last-turn factual query (binary).
   - Cost back-of-envelope: avg tokens saved ~ 40% when using KV; with heuristics we hope to save 30% vs naive full-send but keep success rate within 95% of full-send.

B) Token-cost simulation for Redwood hosted pricing
   - Inputs: avg prompt length 120 tokens, avg response 40 tokens, QPS 50 sustained for test cohort, 10k sessions/day.
   - Baseline cost (full sends) = tokens_per_req * price. Rough numbers: 160 tokens * 10k = 1.6M tokens/day.
   - If caching cuts prompt tokens by 50% we save 800k tokens/day. Price impact depending on tiers — run with realistic per-token price later.

C) Minimal model-side approach: freshness-as-tool-call
   - Tool (external): returns either "stamp: fresh" or "stamp: stale" based on cheap checks. If stale, runtime appends extra context.
   - Pros: no model retrain, deterministic. Cons: extra RTT if tool executed synchronously. Could precompute asynchronously.

Open questions (for experiments / product):
- What is an acceptable outage/failure mode? E.g., one extra hallucination per 10k vs 10% extra cost — customer expectations vary by tier. Map to SLAs for Dedicated.
- Can we cheaply learn threshold T per-customer? (small calibration: 1k supervised labels from their logs)
- How to integrate with rollouts: A/B test freshness heuristics with canary coverage and automatic rollback if quality drops.

Concrete TODOs (next 2 weeks):
- [ ] Pull a 10k-chat anonymized sample from research corpus (ask DataOps for sanitized subset). Owner: Maya.
- [ ] Implement embedding-based freshness script (Ethan) + baseline metrics (latency, token counts, drift metric).
- [ ] Run local sim: cost delta and quality delta for heuristics A/B/C. Capture token-level distribution.
- [ ] Draft short internal one-pager for Product (1–2 pages) describing recommended defaults for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private.

Cheap heuristics I want to test first (priority order):
1) Edit-flag override: if user message contains verbs like "update", "change", "actually" then force full prefix. Very low false negative rate for correction flows.
2) Embedding-delta threshold: cosine(last_turn, rolling_avg) > 0.7 => stale. Tune per workload.
3) Time window: >48 hours since last interaction ⇒ conservative full-send.

Monitoring signals to add to Console (ops notes):
- Freshness-trigger-rate by route/model (how often heuristics fire).
- Quality delta by trigger (automated drift metric; alert if delta > 2% baseline).
- Token-savings visual (stacked by route and by customer).

Mini pseudocode for freshness decision (runtime):
- Input: conversation_id, last_turn_text, rolling_vec, last_activity_ts
- if contains_edit_flag(last_turn_text): return FULL_SEND
- if now - last_activity_ts > 48h: return FULL_SEND
- dist = cos(emb(last_turn_text), rolling_vec)
- if dist < T: return FULL_SEND else return CACHE_REFERENCED_PROMPT

Notes on evaluation label collection (manual):
- Label 500 last-turn factual queries: binary correct/incorrect + hallucination type. Keep sample stratified by time-since-last and user-update flag. Will be used to calibrate T.

Design constraints that matter for productization:
- Latency budgets: heuristics must not add >30ms median overhead in runtime path; embedding checks can be cached/async.
- Privacy: any embeddings for customers in Private must stay in-customer network; design for both hosted and self-hosted.
- Explainability: provide simple per-request reason field (e.g., "freshness=stale:embedding-dist=0.62") for debugging in Console.

Random ideas (parking lot):
- Learn a tiny on-device classifier (2-layer MLP) to predict whether to include prefix. Train on meta-features (time delta, embedding dist, last-turn length).
- Use compressed diffs (ops: diff last important facts and only send changed facts) — requires light NLU extraction.

Immediate next message to core team (draft):
"Short: experimenting with cheap freshness heuristics to reduce token cost while keeping conversational correctness. Pulling sample, will run 3 heuristics and report numbers next week. Would like to pair with Product to define acceptable tradeoffs for Hosted vs Dedicated. - Rohit"

Session notes / random scribbles:
- Example false-positive: user says "Actually, that's wrong" about a prior model hallucination -> edit flag works here.
- Edge case: long multi-party threads where last-turn embedding may be similar but context changed subtly. Might need role-aware embeddings.

End of scratchpad for now. Revisit after experiment run.

-- Rohit
